label: GO after an unrewarded trial when the agent is strongly committed to a1 (early episode)
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (never D1/D2), only when the previous trial was unrewarded (in_rew=0 at D1), and only when the model policy strongly favours a1 (choice logit > 8; every activation has model_act=a1). In practice this is mostly the model-based stay after a rare-unrewarded a1 trial (a1 -> S2 rare, no reward; prev_common=0 carries 80% of mass, prev common = 1 almost never), in episodes where S1 is good (good=S1 83% of mass). It is also tied to episode time: active in trials ~3-49 and silent from trial 50 on, so ep_trial < 45 is part of the predicate. Never fires after a rewarded trial, on a2 choices, or at D1/D2. Uses only observed history plus the agent own policy output; no future variables. Dev F1 0.85, mass recall 0.99. Magnitude was not clearly modulated by any of these variables (recall is flat across activation quartiles), so no magnitude claim is made. Remaining false positives are similar GO steps where it stays silent.

issues: Every factual claim checks out on dev. Activity is 100% at GO and 0 at D1 or D2. prev_reward==1 has 0 activations (test: GO & prev_reward==1 has precision 0). All activations have action a1 / model_act a1. 99.5% of the mass has choice >= 8.07. prev_common=0 holds 80.1% of the mass, prev_common=1 holds 0.7%, and good=S1 holds 82.6%. The ep_trial 40-49 bin has 1085 activations, 50-59 has 9, and 60+ has 0.
The test scores reproduce: precision 0.764, recall 0.954, F1 0.848, mass recall 0.989.

The false positives are not scattered noise. They cluster at the time boundary. Within the predicate, precision is 0.99 for ep_trial<5, 0.84 for 5-35, 0.63 for 35-40, 0.47 for 40-45 and 0.19 for 45-50. The 'early episode' dependence is a gradual fade starting around trial 35, not a sharp cutoff at 45. The explanation's 'silent from trial 50 on' is right, but treating 45 as a boundary overstates how crisp the cutoff is. Moving the cutoff to 40 or 42 only trades recall for precision (dev F1 0.844 and 0.853; test F1 at 42 is 0.845).

No better fix turned up. Raising the choice threshold (>9: F1 0.838; >10: F1 0.660), adding tv('reward',-2), prev_common!=1 (F1 0.849) or good!=2 (F1 0.842), or trading choice linearly against ep_trial (best F1 0.815) all fail to beat the original. The leftover ~16% false positives inside trials 5-35 have no visible pattern in reward, transition or good state.

Minor: all activation mass sits in the value bin [7.73, 8.10). This is probably a correlate of strong a1 commitment, not an independent driver: adding the value window to prev_reward==0 & choice>8 gives F1 0.76, and value alone with prev_reward==0 gives F1 0.39. Label and explanation are not wrong on this point, just incomplete.
